lexemes.fix: Deck gave 얼마나 for 'how many'; 얼마나 asks about degree (how long, how far). Counting things uses 몇 개 (extra).
학교 is 'school'; the deck's 'université' is 대학교.
Deck mixed two words: 낮 is 'daytime', 오후 is 'afternoon (p.m.)'; split into entry + extra.
시간 is 'time' or 'hours' of duration; the clock hour ('three o'clock') uses 시.
공부하다 is 'to study'; 'to learn' (apprendre) is 배우다.

lexemes.english: to get on, to ride (a vehicle)

lexemes.fix: Deck had the templates '...이에요 / ...예요'; cleaned to 이에요 (after a consonant); 예요 is the same ending after a vowel.
Deck had the template '...에 있어요'; cleaned to 에 있어요 (place + 에 있어요).

lexemes.fix: Deck had the templates '...하고 / ...와/과'; cleaned to 하고, with 와 (과 after a consonant) as the written-style extra.
Deck had the template '...고 싶어요'; cleaned to 고 싶어요 (verb stem + 고 싶어요).
Deck had the template '...(으)ㄹ 수 있어요'; cleaned to 수 있어요 (stem + ㄹ/을 수 있어요, e.g. 먹을 수 있어요).
Deck's '...못 해요' was misleading: 못 goes right before the verb (못 가요, 못 먹어요); 못 해요 alone means 'I can't do it'.
Spacing normalized from 말해주세요 to the standard 말해 주세요 (the attached form is also tolerated).

lexemes.english: thank you for the meal (said before eating)
thank you for the meal (said after eating)

lexemes.fix: Means 'you can do it! / go for it!' (a cheer), not a wish of luck; the dictionary spelling is 파이팅.
제발 is pleading ('please, I beg you'), not the everyday polite 'please'; requests use 주세요 or -아/어 주세요.
Spacing: 그다음 is a single dictionary word, so the deck's 그 다음 is written 그다음.
Deck had Arabic فقط with 'bak-kke'; replaced by the particle 만 ('only'); 밖에 (extra) also means 'only' but needs a negative verb.
흐림 is the weather-forecast noun ('cloudy'); in speech use the adjective 흐리다 → 흐려요 (extra).

lexemes.english: to get up (from bed or a seat)

lexemes.fix: 씻다 is for washing the body, hands, food or dishes; washing clothes is 빨래하다.
사 드리다 is the honorific 'buy for someone older or senior', not just 'buy as a gift'.
시도해요 is stiff and written; everyday 'try' is -아/어 보다 (해 봐요, 먹어 봐요, 입어 봐요).
변경해요 is stiff and administrative; the everyday verb for 'to change' is 바꾸다 (바꿔요).

to be boring, to be tedious
to be new, to be fresh (novel)
lexemes.fix: 새롭다 means 'new, fresh, novel'; for a new object use the determiner 새 before the noun (extra): 새 차.

lexemes.english: to grow old, to be old (age)
lexemes.fix: 늙다 is blunt about people; politely say 나이가 많으세요 ('he/she is older').
Deck glossed 딱딱하다 as 'difficult'; it means physically hard or rigid. 'Difficult' is 어렵다 (row 123, 어려워요).
가득하다 is one word, so 가득 해요 is written 가득해요; in speech 가득 차 있어요 is more common.

Deck glossed 거짓말 as 'false'; it is the noun 'a lie' (거짓말하다 'to lie'). 'Wrong, false' is 틀리다.
